title.en: Climate of India: factors, monsoon and seasons

text.en: When Chennai bakes at 35 degrees, Ooty is comfortably cool. Why do places so close in India have such different weather? The answer lies in the factors that shape climate.

Weather is the state of the atmosphere of a place at a given time; climate is the accumulation of daily and seasonal weather events over 30 to 35 years.
India's climate is controlled by latitude, altitude, distance from the sea, monsoon winds, relief and jet streams.
India lies between 8 degrees 4 minutes N and 37 degrees 6 minutes N, and the Tropic of Cancer divides it into two halves; the south has an equable climate.
Temperature falls 6.5 degrees Celsius for every 1000 metres of ascent, the normal lapse rate, so hill stations are cool.
Coastal places like Kochi have equable climate while interior places like Delhi have extremes; Kolkata gets 119 cm of rain but Bikaner only 24 cm.
The word monsoon comes from the Arabic mausim, meaning season; monsoon winds reverse their direction with the seasons.
India has four seasons: winter (January-February), summer (March-May), southwest monsoon (June-September) and northeast monsoon (October-December).
Summer brings Mango Showers on the west coast and Norwesters or Kalbaisakhis in the east and northeast.
The southwest monsoon arrives at the southern tip in the first week of June, covers the whole country by 15 July and gives about 75 percent of the rainfall.
Its Arabian Sea branch drenches the windward Western Ghats, while its Bay of Bengal branch gives Mawsynram, the wettest place in the world.
The retreating monsoon returns over the Bay of Bengal and, deflected by the Coriolis force, blows from the northeast, giving Tamil Nadu 35 percent of its annual rain.

problem.en: Why does Mangalore get 280 cm of rain in the southwest monsoon while Bengaluru gets only 50 cm?

text.en: Mangalore lies on the windward side of the Western Ghats.

why.en: Moist winds are forced to rise.

text.en: Rising air cools and drops its moisture as heavy rain.
Bengaluru is in the rain shadow on the leeward side.
So relief explains the difference in rainfall.

prompt.en: Explain how altitude and distance from the sea together make Ooty and Chennai different.

requiredIdeas.en: Ooty is at 2240 m so it is cooler by the lapse rate (about 14 degrees less)
Chennai is on the coast at 6.7 m, so it is warm and humid
Altitude controls temperature, the sea adds humidity

points.en: Six factors: latitude, altitude, distance from sea, monsoon, relief, jet streams.
Four seasons, SW monsoon gives 75 percent of rain.
NE monsoon brings rain to Tamil Nadu.
